column1: # Checklist corpus expectations (arbsec/orchestraitor#799 R3).
# ONE table for the whole corpus: each `<nn>-<slug>.md` body in this directory
# has exactly one row here, keyed by its FILE STEM. Both engines read it —
# `scripts/test-reconcile-checklist` (f5) and the Rust test
# `checklist_corpus_matches_both_engines` in
# `crates/orchestraitor-mcp/src/pr_status.rs` — so a divergence in either fence
# scanner fails CI. One table instead of a `.expected` file per case keeps the
# corpus reviewable: 75 cases x 2 files is 151 files, past the reviewer's limit.
# Columns, TAB separated:
#   1. case                   the `<nn>-<slug>` file stem of the `.md` body
#   2. marker_count           managed markers the scanner counts in the body
#   3. all_checked            `true` only when every counted marker is ticked AND
#                             the reading is determinate
#   4. unparseable            `true` when the reading is REFUSED; omitted (and
#                             therefore false) unless the case pins it
#   5. unparseable_construct  `indented_fence_opener`, `html_construct`,
#                             `indented_marker` or `near_marker`; present only
#                             with column 4
# A case file with NO row fails BOTH suites, and a row with NO case file fails
# both suites: a deleted case can never narrow the contract silently. The case
# count is pinned exactly (`CORPUS_FLOOR`) in both suites too.
# HTML is NOT MODELLED (#799 R1): a line OUTSIDE every fenced code region whose
# FIRST non-whitespace character is `<`, indented 0-3 spaces, makes the reading
# indeterminate (`html_construct`) and blocks. A 4+-space-indented (or tab-led)
# line is literal indented code and hides nothing; a `<` mid-line (`x < y`) is
# ordinary text; a line inside a fenced region is inert. Deliberately stricter
# than CommonMark — #809 tracks real modelling. Every case whose expectation was
# re-derived for that rule says so in its own comment.
# prose that only MENTIONS the marker syntax carries no checklist item. Its
# `<!--` is mid-line, and only a line-START `<` is a refusal (#799 R1), so the
# prose is visible text — not evidence either way.
01-no-markers
# KNOWN GAP arbsec/orchestraitor#800: the gate checks only the markers it FINDS, so one ticked marker satisfies it.
02-one-checked-marker-800
# the nine managed template markers, all unticked.
03-nine-unchecked
# the nine managed template markers, all ticked.
04-nine-checked
# the nine managed template markers, exactly one unticked.
05-one-unchecked-among-nine
# a marker inside a closed backtick fence is an example, not evidence.
06-marker-in-backtick-fence
# a marker inside a closed tilde fence is an example, not evidence.
07-marker-in-tilde-fence
# an unclosed backtick fence runs to the end of the body.
08-unclosed-backtick-fence
# an unclosed tilde fence runs to the end of the body (a backtick line is content, not a closer).
09-unclosed-tilde-fence
# a tilde fence may contain backtick lines; only the marker AFTER the tilde closer counts.
10-tilde-fence-with-backticks
# A backtick fence may contain tilde lines; only the marker AFTER the backtick closer counts.
# The fenced marker is UNCHECKED on purpose: a parser that wrongly counted it would see two
# items with one unticked, so this case separates "ignored the fenced marker" from "counted
# it and ignored the real one".
11-backtick-fence-with-tildes
# a closer longer than the opener closes the region.
12-closer-longer-than-opener
# a closer shorter than the opener does not close the region.
13-closer-shorter-than-opener
# a closer with trailing spaces still closes (only whitespace may follow it).
14-closer-trailing-spaces
# a closer with an info string does not close the region.
15-closer-with-info-string
# F16: a 4-space-indented run is indented code, never an opener, so the marker counts.
16-four-space-opener-is-text
# F16: a 4-space-indented run is never a closer, so the enclosed marker stays hidden.
# The case is RENAMED to say so (four CodeRabbit generations raised the same
# "case 17 has an open fence" claim, and the rationale alone did not stop it):
# the fence is CLOSED. The file's own comment names the lines: line 6 is the
# column-0 OPENER, line 7 is the 4-space-indented run (literal CONTENT, never a
# closer), line 8 is the marker inside the region, and **line 9 is the real
# column-0 CLOSER** -- the marker on line 8 is an EXAMPLE, which is why
# marker_count is 0.
17-four-space-run-does-not-close-the-fence
# arbsec/orchestraitor#809: a fence OPENER indented 1-3 spaces may equally
# belong to a list item or a block quote, and the scanner has no container
# model. The condition is STICKY — it is NOT cleared when the region closes,
# because a closer at a different container level ends the region EARLIER for
# the renderer than for this scanner, so a marker swallowed by the scanner's
# region can still be VISIBLE to a human. Every 1-3-space opener is therefore
# refused (`checklist_unparseable`) and `all_checked` is false, closed or not
# (corpus case 48 is the swallowed-item shape this rule protects). Only the
# marker after the region is visible, and it is ticked. A 0-space opener is
# modelled exactly as before, and 4+ spaces is literal indented code.
18-three-space-opener-is-indeterminate
# a tab-indented run reaches the 4-column tab stop: literal text, so the marker counts.
19-tab-indented-line-is-text
# F17: ```example``` is a closed inline code span, not an opener, so the marker counts.
20-inline-closed-span-is-not-an-opener
# F17: a backtick in a backtick fence info string means NOT an opener, so the marker counts.
21-backtick-in-info-string-unclosed-is-not-an-opener
# a marker after a closed fence counts.
22-marker-after-closed-fence
# a marker before a fence counts.
23-marker-before-fence
# two fences in sequence: the marker after both counts.
24-two-fences-in-sequence
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): the column-0 `<!--` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT, so the reading is
# REFUSED (`unparseable: true`, `html_construct`) instead of modelling the comment — and
# the fence inside it is now a REAL region, which swallows the item after it (0 markers).
# Blocking is the contract; the count is not derived from it.
25-fence-inside-html-comment
# CRLF line endings: fences and markers parse exactly as with LF.
26-crlf-line-endings
# no trailing newline on the last marker line: it still counts.
27-no-trailing-newline
# the literal orc:none sentinel inside a fence is inert content.
28-sentinel-inside-fence-is-inert
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): a bare `<!-- orc:none -->` sentinel still waives NOTHING. It is
# now a line-start `<` RAW HTML CONSTRUCT, so the reading is REFUSED (`html_construct`)
# rather than falling through to `checklist_markers_missing`: stricter, never a waiver.
29-bare-sentinel-waives-nothing
# only the marker OUTSIDE the fence counts (and it is unchecked).
30-marker-inside-and-outside-fence
# a fence with no checklist markers at all.
31-fence-only-no-markers
# an uppercase X box is a checked item.
32-uppercase-checked-box
# a different fence character never closes a region.
# The two in-region markers are UNCHECKED on purpose: a parser that wrongly closes at
# `~~~` reports two unticked items, so the case separates "the tilde line is content"
# from "the region closed early" — the same discrimination case 11 gained.
33-different-fence-char-never-closes
# a marker on the first line inside a fence is hidden.
34-marker-immediately-after-opener
# F18: a vertical tab after the closer is NOT fence-tail whitespace, so the region stays open
# and the checked marker after it is an EXAMPLE, not evidence (GitHub renders it as code).
35-vt-after-closer-is-not-whitespace
# Re-derive corpus case 36: a vertical-tab-led marker line is prose for the
# CANONICAL grammar, but it still carries a task-item box token AND an
# `orc:NAME` reference — so under the near-marker rule it is INDETERMINATE, not
# merely skipped (arbsec/orchestraitor#799 R1).
# F18: only space and tab indent a checklist item, so a VT-led marker line is
# not a canonical checklist item in BOTH engines. It is not skipped silently,
# though: it presents a managed marker the canonical grammar cannot read (a
# task-item box token plus an `orc:NAME` reference), so the reading is
# REFUSED — `unparseable` is true and the verdict blocks with
# `checklist_unparseable`. The real item after it is still the only counted
# marker.
36-vt-led-marker-line-is-not-an-item
# CommonMark 0.31: a closing code fence may be followed only by spaces or tabs, so a form feed
# after the closer is CONTENT, not fence-tail whitespace: the region stays OPEN and the checked
# marker behind it is an EXAMPLE, not evidence. (Rust's `is_ascii_whitespace` admits `\f`; the
# spec does not. Corpus case 35 pins the same rule for a vertical tab.)
37-form-feed-after-closer-is-not-whitespace
# F18: a fence opens only after 0-3 spaces, never after a vertical tab, so a VT-led fence line
# opens nothing and the checked marker below it is a real item in BOTH engines.
38-vt-led-fence-opener-is-not-a-fence
# CommonMark §2.1: a lone CR is a line ending and so is CRLF, normalised to LF ONCE
# before parsing. The first CR ends the fence line, the CRLF ends an empty line, so
# the closer CLOSES. Rust and the shell used to disagree here (gen-7).
39-cr-crlf-after-closer
# A body whose ONLY line ending is a lone CR: CommonMark §2.1 normalises it to LF,
# so fences and markers parse exactly as with LF. Without normalisation the whole
# body is ONE line, the opener never closes and marker_count is 0.
40-lone-cr-line-endings
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): the line-start `<!--` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT, so the reading is
# REFUSED (`html_construct`). The deleted comment model would have hidden the marker
# inside it; with no model every line is text, so all three markers count — and no
# verdict is derived from a count on a refused reading.
41-marker-inside-html-comment
# A `<!--` inside an inline code span is LITERAL TEXT: only a line-START `<` is
# a refusal (#799 R1), so the token changes nothing and the visible unchecked
# item after it is still evidence. An engine that treated ANY `<!--` as a
# construct would refuse (or hide) a body that plainly carries an unticked item
# — the fail-open defect this case pins.
42-inline-code-comment-token
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): a `<!--` at the START of a line is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT, so the
# reading is REFUSED (`html_construct`) instead of opening a comment. Both markers count
# as text; the gate blocks on the refusal, never on that count.
43-line-start-comment-opens
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): the `<!--` opener is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED
# (`html_construct`). The closer restores nothing because no comment is modelled: every
# line is text, and the body blocks on the refusal.
44-comment-closer-restores-visibility
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): an UNCLOSED comment is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED
# (`html_construct`) rather than modelled to EOF. The fail-closed property survives: the
# body can never be read as a pass.
45-unclosed-comment-runs-to-end
# A TAB between the box and the marker delimiter is NOT the canonical form
# (the separators are exactly one ASCII space), so this line is a NEAR-MARKER:
# it carries a task-item box token AND an orc:NAME reference, and the gate
# cannot tell what it asserts. The reading is INDETERMINATE — the line is not
# counted as an item and the verdict blocks with `checklist_unparseable`.
# The old expectation counted the line as an ordinary item (the whitespace-class
# grammar the canonical form replaces).
46-marker-with-tab-after-box
# arbsec/orchestraitor#809: an opener indented 1-3 spaces may equally belong to
# a list item or a block quote, and the scanner has no container model. While
# that region is OPEN the scope is INDETERMINATE, so the reading is refused and
# `all_checked` is false even though the only visible marker is ticked (the
# verdict blocks with `checklist_unparseable`). The region never closes in THIS
# case, but closing is not what makes it indeterminate: the rule is STICKY, so a
# region that DOES close is refused in exactly the same way (corpus case 18 pins
# the 3-space closed shape, case 48 the 2-space one).
47-unclosed-indented-opener-is-indeterminate
# The case a "closing clears the condition" rule gets WRONG. CommonMark ends the
# fence at the end of the list item, so the `- [ ]` line is OUTSIDE the fence
# and visible in the rendered PR; this scanner's region runs on to the final
# closer, so it swallows that item. The region DOES close here, and a rule that
# cleared the indeterminate condition on a close would report one ticked marker
# and no unticked one — a false pass on evidence a human can see is missing.
# The 2-space opener is therefore refused (`checklist_unparseable`) and
# `all_checked` is false, closed or not (corpus case 18 is the symmetric
# 3-space shape; case 47 is the unclosed one).
48-closed-indented-opener-is-indeterminate
# A NO-BREAK SPACE between the box and the marker delimiter is not the
# canonical form: the separators are exactly one ASCII space. The line carries
# a task-item box token AND an orc:NAME reference, so it is a NEAR-MARKER and
# the reading is INDETERMINATE — the verdict blocks with
# `checklist_unparseable` and the line is NOT counted as an item.
49-near-marker-nbsp-after-box
# A NO-BREAK SPACE inside the marker token (`<!--` and `orc:security`) is
# not the canonical form either. The near-marker detection is a plain
# substring search for `orc:NAME` — no whitespace class is involved — so the
# line is recognised as a managed-marker reference and the reading is
# INDETERMINATE.
50-near-marker-nbsp-inside-the-token
# A TAB after the box is not the canonical form (exactly one ASCII space).
# The line is a NEAR-MARKER, so the reading is INDETERMINATE and the verdict
# blocks with `checklist_unparseable`.
51-near-marker-tab-after-box
# TWO spaces after the box are not the canonical form (exactly one ASCII
# space). The line is a NEAR-MARKER, so the reading is INDETERMINATE and the
# verdict blocks with `checklist_unparseable`.
52-near-marker-two-spaces-after-box
# A box character other than `x`, `X` or a single space is not the
# canonical form. The line still carries a task-item box token AND an
# `orc:NAME` reference, so it is a NEAR-MARKER: a malformed managed marker is
# something the gate must not silently ignore. The reading is INDETERMINATE
# and the verdict blocks with `checklist_unparseable`.
53-near-marker-box-char-other-than-x
# A managed marker behind a block-quote prefix is not the canonical form: the
# indent class is SPACES and TABS, so `>` makes the line a NEAR-MARKER. The
# reading is INDETERMINATE and the verdict blocks with
# `checklist_unparseable`.
54-near-marker-blockquote-prefixed
# A line that mentions `orc:NAME` but carries NO task-item box token is
# PROSE, not a managed marker: it is not a near-marker, so it never blocks.
# Only the canonical marker counts. A gate that blocked on prose would make
# the checklist unusable.
55-prose-mentions-orc-name-without-a-box
# A task-item box token with NO `orc:NAME` reference is a PLAIN TASK, not a
# managed marker: it is not a near-marker, so it never blocks and it is not
# counted. Only the canonical marker counts.
56-plain-task-without-orc
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): `<pre>` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED (`html_construct`).
# The fence inside it is a real fenced region now (no HTML extent encloses it), so it
# swallows the item after it (1 marker). Nothing is guessed: the reading is refused.
57-html-block-pre-fence-inside
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): `<pre>` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED (`html_construct`). No
# block extent is modelled, so both markers count as text; no verdict uses that count.
58-html-block-pre-marker-inside
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): `<details>` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED (`html_construct`).
# The blank-line-terminated extent is deleted, so both markers count as text.
59-html-block-details-ends-at-blank-line
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): `<script>` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED (`html_construct`).
# The closing-tag extent is deleted, so both markers count as text.
60-html-block-script-runs-to-closing-tag
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): the line-start `<!--` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED
# (`html_construct`). No comment is modelled, so a marker's own `-->` closes nothing and
# both markers count as text.
61-marker-closer-ends-the-comment

# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): `
` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED
# (`html_construct`). The one-line type-1 model is deleted; the body blocks on the
# refusal whatever the marker count says (ten here).
62-html-type1-closes-on-opening-line
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): `<!-->` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED (`html_construct`).
# The degenerate-terminator model is deleted; the marker below counts as text.
# TWO REVIEW GENERATIONS asked whether the marker on line 2 is a rendered task: it is
# NOT, and the concern cannot occur — the expectation is `1 false true html_construct`,
# i.e. the reading is REFUSED, so `all_checked` is false and no verdict reads that marker
# as evidence. The count is reported for the record only.
63-html-comment-empty-terminator
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): an AUTOLINK is ordinary text in CommonMark, but this scanner
# does not model HTML at all — a line-start `<` is REFUSED (`html_construct`). It is
# deliberately STRICTER than CommonMark, and #809 tracks real modelling.
64-autolink-is-not-a-block
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): INLINE HTML is ordinary text in CommonMark, but a line-start `<`
# is REFUSED (`html_construct`). Deliberately stricter; #809 tracks real modelling.
65-inline-html-is-not-a-block
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): an INCOMPLETE tag is ordinary text in CommonMark, but a
# line-start `<` is REFUSED (`html_construct`). Deliberately stricter; #809 tracks it.
66-incomplete-tag-is-not-a-block
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): `<?xml` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED (`html_construct`).
# The processing-instruction extent is deleted, so the nine markers count as text (9);
# the body blocks on the refusal, not on `checklist_markers_missing`.
67-html-type3-processing-instruction
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): `<![CDATA[` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED (`html_construct`).
# The CDATA extent is deleted, so the nine markers count as text (9).
68-html-type5-cdata-section
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): `<div>` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED (`html_construct`). The
# blank-line extent is deleted, so both markers count as text.
69-html-type6-ends-at-blank-line
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): an unclosed `<pre>` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED
# (`html_construct`). No to-EOF extent is modelled; the marker counts as text.
70-html-type1-unclosed-runs-to-eof
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): an INDENTED opener is the SAME refusal as a column-0 one — a
# line-start `<` in the 0-3 space window is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT (`html_construct`), never
# a separate container-ambiguity construct. Its marker counts as text.
71-html-indented-opener-is-indeterminate
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): a COMPLETE tag alone on its line is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT —
# REFUSED (`html_construct`). The type-7 extent is deleted, so both markers count.
72-html-type7-complete-tag-only
# The delivery lane's denial-of-progress vector (arbsec/orchestraitor#799 R4): a
# model summary line with a TAB after the box is NOT the canonical managed
# marker, but it carries BOTH a task-item box token and an `orc:NAME` reference,
# so every scanner REFUSES the whole reading (`checklist_unparseable`). Ticking
# the nine managed boxes does not remove the line, so a body composed from this
# summary can never converge. The lane therefore neutralises the line (see
# `delivery_clears_a_near_marker_in_the_summary`); this case pins the reading of
# the RAW summary that makes the neutralisation necessary.
# The two further vectors this lane used to defer are BOTH closed by the
# line-start `<` escape (arbsec/orchestraitor#810, now closed): an INDENTED HTML
# opener sits in exactly the scanner's 0-3-space refusal window, so it is escaped
# like a column-0 one, and no block extent is modelled any more, so an UNCLOSED
# raw HTML block has nothing to extend — the opener line is the only thing to
# neutralise. Pinned by `delivery_escapes_a_line_start_html_construct_in_the_summary`
# (arbsec/orchestraitor#810, closed).
73-near-marker-in-a-delivery-summary
# The DESCRIPTION of a managed marker is the text AFTER `-->`, for a checked and
# an unchecked item alike. `reconcile-checklist --json` emitted the BOX character
# here (`"x"` / `""`) because its sed emitted group 1 instead of group 2, while
# the Rust engine returned the text — a cross-engine divergence in a field
# `pr status` publishes (arbsec/orchestraitor#799 R2). The two counts are pinned
# here; the description VALUES are asserted by `test-reconcile-checklist`
# (`f8c`) and by `descriptions_are_the_text_after_the_delimiter` in both engines.
74-description-text
# RE-DERIVED (#799 R1): `<!--->` is a RAW HTML CONSTRUCT — REFUSED (`html_construct`).
# The degenerate-terminator model is deleted; the marker below counts as text.
75-html-comment-dash-terminator
# arbsec/orchestraitor#802, CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION: nine canonical ticked markers,
# each preceded by FOUR spaces and with no surrounding list, render entirely as an
# INDENTED CODE BLOCK — yet the gate used to report `marker_count=9,
# all_checked=true` and the merge lane merged it. The canonical grammar's leading
# `[ \t]*` cannot distinguish "marker inside a list item" (legitimate) from
# "standalone indented code" (not evidence), and neither scanner has a container
# model, so the reading is REFUSED (`indented_marker`) instead of guessed. The
# markers still COUNT: `marker_count` is a pure function of the canonical grammar,
# and the verdict blocks on the refusal, never on that count.
76-nine-four-space-indented-markers
# The same refusal does not depend on the body carrying nothing else: nine
# 4-space-indented markers PLUS the nine canonical column-0 ones are still
# indeterminate — the indented line is refused wherever it sits, and the count
# (18) is not read.
77-four-space-indented-plus-canonical
# The inverse, and the legitimate case: 0-3 leading spaces is a marker nested in
# a list item, so nine 2-space-indented ticked markers are ACCEPTED exactly as
# before (`marker_count` 9, `all_checked` true).
78-two-space-indented-markers
# A TAB-led marker reaches the 4-column tab stop, so it is the same refusal as a
# 4-space indent (`indented_marker`), and the line still counts as a canonical
# marker. Never silently dropped: a body whose only marker is this one blocks on
# the refusal, not on `checklist_markers_missing`.
79-tab-led-marker
# A NEAR-MARKER indented 4 spaces is indeterminate for BOTH reasons; the reported
# construct is `indented_marker`, because the indentation is what makes it
# render as code (the construct list resolves a same-line tie to the more
# specific rule). The nine column-0 markers still count. This row is
# `9 false true indented_marker` on purpose: the reading is REFUSED, so the
# fixture is NOT a question about list nesting and NOT an acceptance case --
# every ticked box in it is irrelevant while the line stays indented.
80-four-space-indented-near-marker
# arbsec/orchestraitor#799 R12, the LOCALE-INDEPENDENCE pin: a box token is `[` +
# exactly ONE CHARACTER + `]`, and the shell decoder reads one UTF-8 sequence by
# BYTE in the C locale while the Rust engine counts one `char`. `[✓] orc:review`
# is therefore a NEAR-MARKER in BOTH engines on every machine — without this pin,
# a box whose `C.UTF-8` probe failed read the three-byte `✓` as three characters
# and let the line through as prose while Rust refused it (a false pass).
81-unicode-box-token-without-a-comment
# The same pin with the delimiter present: `[✓]  <!-- orc:tests -->` is a
# near-marker (non-canonical spacing) in both engines, in every locale.
82-unicode-box-token-before-a-comment
# arbsec/orchestraitor#799 R15: a box token is `[` + exactly ONE character + `]`,
# and `]` IS a legal middle character: `[]]` has the first `]` as its middle and
# the second as its closer, so this line is a NEAR-MARKER (not prose) and the
# reading is REFUSED. `[]` is still not a token, because nothing follows the pair.
# NOTE: `[]]` is not a rendered GFM checkbox, so this is a near-marker DETECTION
# gap, not a false pass of rendered evidence.
83-box-token-is-a-bracket
# arbsec/orchestraitor#799 R16: a DESCRIPTION may contain a TAB. The shell engine used to
# pass items through a tab-delimited intermediate, so the field split truncated
# `alpha<TAB>beta` to `alpha` while the Rust engine returned the full text. The item is
# built with `jq --arg` now, so no byte of the body can collide with the encoding; the
# full description is asserted by BOTH engines (the shell suite and the Rust
# `descriptions_are_the_text_after_the_delimiter` test).
84-description-with-a-tab
